title: fix(invoke): rhx drops skill stderr on a successful run
description:
## .what

`rhx <skill>` drops every byte a skill writes to stderr when the skill exits 0.

## .where

`src/domain.operations/invoke/executeSkill.ts` runs the skill via `spawnSync` with
`stdio: [process.stdin, process.stdout, 'pipe']` in stream mode. the piped stderr is read only
to build `SkillExecutionError` on a non-zero exit. on exit 0 it is discarded.

## .why it hurts

- a progress line on stderr never reaches the human. `rhx review._.cost --of grove` writes its
  per-tree progress to stderr (so `--json` stays pure on stdout), and via `rhx` it ran over ten
  minutes with zero output: a silent wait a human cannot tell from a hang
  (rule.require.status-feedback)
- any caution a skill prints on stderr on a successful run vanishes — a failhide
- even on a failure, naught streams: stderr is replayed only after the skill exits

## .the shape of the fix

1. in stream mode, inherit stderr: `stdio: [process.stdin, process.stdout, process.stderr]`.
   the human then sees each stderr byte live, on success and on failure alike
2. `SkillExecutionError.stderr` becomes null in stream mode (the bytes already reached the
   terminal), so the error render must not depend on it there. capture mode keeps the pipe
3. clamp: an integration test with a skill that writes `progress` to stderr and exits 0;
   assert the bytes reach the parent's stderr. red today, green after

## .found

dogfood of `rhx review._.cost --of grove` in rhachet-roles-bhrain, 2026-10-16.
